name: ci-cancel-and-docs-skip
title: CI: cancel superseded PR runs and skip the build legs on docs-only changes
issue: Analysis and decisions: C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/ci-speedup.md (read it fully first: measured per-leg times, critical path, the queueing finding, risks). The user APPROVED (2026-10-15): (1) the cheap workflow-only change below; (2) Linux ccache AFTER that, then decide on Windows after measuring; (3) ALL 8 legs stay on every PR (do NOT remove or move any leg, do NOT rename any job: the required check is `linux (Release, x86_64, Clang)`, the other jobs are `linux (Release, x86_64, GCC 14)`, `linux (Release, arm64, Clang)`, `windows (Debug, PhysX ON)`, `windows (Release, PhysX ON)`, `windows (Debug, PhysX OFF, FreeType ON, ufbx ON, TLS ON)`, `docker (editor host image, x86_64)`, `protocol (generated clients, golden vectors)`). Constraints: workflow-only changes (.github/workflows/), no source changes; nothing can be tested locally: the PR's own CI run is the test, so write the YAML defensively, re-read it for syntax/indentation, and prefer GitHub's documented semantics (verify them in your head against docs you know: concurrency groups, job-level `if`, `needs`, skipped-job handling for required checks (a job skipped by a job-level `if` reports 'skipped' and a skipped required check counts as passing; a skipped job whose `needs` failed does NOT), `fromJSON`, cache action rules (caches created on a PR ref are not readable by sibling PRs; the default branch cache is readable by PRs)). The orchestrator's own tooling polls check-runs by head sha and treats conclusions `failure|cancelled|timed_out` as failed and counts `completed` runs: a superseded run that gets cancelled is expected; a skipped job is fine; do not rely on anything else. Do NOT touch the merge gates or ratify tooling. SCOPE: edit .github/workflows/tests.yml (and only it unless another workflow clearly needs the same concurrency rule: check physx-linux.yml and physx-windows-slim.yml: they are dry runs on PR and publish only by dispatch/tag: do NOT cancel publish/dispatch/tag runs). (1) Add a `concurrency` block to the Tests workflow with a group keyed on the PR/branch (e.g. `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}`) and `cancel-in-progress` ONLY for pull_request events (e.g. `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}`) so pushes to master, workflow_dispatch and tag runs are never cancelled; think through what happens when the orchestrator does `update-branch` or pushes a fix while an older head is still running (the older run is cancelled: intended). (2) Add a cheap first job (e.g. `changes`, runs-on ubuntu-latest, no checkout of dependencies: checkout with fetch-depth 0 or use the GitHub API via `gh`/`git diff`) that decides `docs_only` = true when the PR's changed files (base...head, for pull_request events only; for push/dispatch/tag always false) ALL match docs/** or *.md at the repo root (and nothing else: tests/, deploy/, lua_project/, CMake, source, .github/ are NOT docs-only; an edit of .github/workflows/** is never docs-only), exposed as a job output; implement the file classification with plain git/shell (do NOT add a third-party paths-filter action). (3) Make the 7 build/test jobs `needs: changes` with a job-level `if: needs.changes.outputs.docs_only != 'true'` so docs-only PRs skip them in about a minute while the job NAMES (the check names) stay EXACTLY the same; keep the `protocol` job running always (cheap) or skip it as well on docs-only: pick the safer (keep running); make sure a failure of the `changes` job itself cannot silently skip required checks as success (a skipped job whose needs FAILED is skipped, and a failed `changes` job shows red: acceptable, but document it); if `changes` is red the PR must not look green. (4) Docs: add a short paragraph to docs/testing.html (CI section) describing the concurrency cancel and the docs-only skip, and the exact docs-only rule. (5) Unverified items to list: the docs-only path cannot be exercised by this PR's own run (it changes .github/ so it is NOT docs-only); say so, and describe the first docs-only PR as the proof; also whether GitHub treats the skipped jobs as satisfying the required check once branch protection is enabled (documented behaviour; not testable here). Nothing builds locally; the PR's CI run (8 checks) is the test.
acceptance: All 8 checks still run with unchanged names on a PR that touches code or workflows
Superseded PR runs are cancelled; master/dispatch/tag runs are never cancelled
A docs-only PR skips the 7 build/test jobs (rule documented); the `changes` job cannot make a bad PR look green
No leg removed or renamed; docs/testing.html describes the rules
notes: Reviewer: step through the YAML as GitHub would: concurrency expression for each event type, the docs_only computation for pull_request/push/dispatch/tag, job names unchanged, needs/if wiring (skipped vs failed semantics), no accidental cancellation of master runs, fetch-depth/base-ref handling for the diff, shell quoting. Unverified: the docs-only skip path (first docs-only PR proves it), required-check behaviour of skipped jobs with branch protection.
